about: Section 13 of spec.md, the acceptance table, as the final gate of step 7: each row's completion evidence is the tests named here, by file and a pattern of their names. node tools/acceptance.mjs runs every file once (the browser checks in each browser project named, all five by default) and passes a row only when each piece of evidence matched a test that passed, and failed none; the browser evidence must pass in every project it names.

rows.evidence: A fresh import produces figures and an export package without chart selection or a known question.

tests.name: the whole workflow: a file chosen

rows.evidence: Fixtures show preserved source values, reported parse failures, and explicit conversions.

tests.name: ^data integrity: source values are kept as written
^data integrity: parse failures, impossible dates, markers and sentinels
^approval: an approved correction changes the reading

rows.evidence: Fixtures cover each supported operation and verify results, including nulls and duplicate join keys.

tests.name: ^one fixture per operation of spec.md section 4

rows.evidence: Small fixtures produce the expected complete candidate set for the documented grammar.

tests.name: ^the exact candidate set of a small table

rows.evidence: Every generated candidate has an explicit outcome. Exclusions include reasons.

tests.name: ^field classes: Q, C, T and L, and every exclusion with its reason
^the planted example: 155 candidates, each with an outcome

rows.evidence: Known unusual patterns appear in the unusual-pattern list. Distinct highlights include explanations.

tests.name: ^discovery: the planted patterns lead the unusual-pattern list

rows.evidence: Reference cases verify test selection, assumptions, effect sizes, and BY correction.

tests.name: ^the page.s SQL gives the reference statistics
^independence: a repeated identifier and serial correlation

rows.evidence: Synthetic null datasets verify false-discovery behavior under the stated assumptions.
Format checks and visual inspection verify editable artwork and legibility at final size.

tests.name: ^the general preset: every chart kind meets its checks as PDF and SVG
^the PDF keeps rotated, anchored and bold text as text
^the checks fail on small or coloured text
^charts: every candidate of the planted example

rows.evidence: Every enforced rule has a journal-specific source and a verification date.

tests.name: ^every preset rule names its journal stage, source and date

rows.evidence: The tested parser accepts the document, and the renderer displays its figures correctly.
Fixtures cover point events, intervals, uncertain dates, and duplicate events.

tests.name: ^timelines: dates known to the year or month

rows.evidence: A saved project reproduces figures and statistical results with the recorded inputs and settings.

tests.name: ^a saved project made again from the same bytes

rows.evidence: Real-browser tests complete the full workflow with touch input and mobile downloads.

tests.name: ^the export package: one download \(by touch on a phone\)

rows.evidence: Benchmarks state devices, browsers, dataset sizes, elapsed times, and resource limits.

tests.name: ^benchmark: import, profile and every candidate of the 50-column table
^the typed copy gives the same figures and statistics

rows.evidence: Cancellation and resource-limit tests preserve results and report incomplete work accurately.

tests.name: ^resource limit: a query beyond the engine
^the memory limit and Cancel each stop the ladder
^completion: charts or statistics that did not finish
^a file too large for the budget is refused before import; Cancel keeps nothing
